nonblocking_findings: F3 [Nit] phase-acceptance: Line plan.md:16 says `All suites and both parity checks pass`, but plan.md:19 records that `bun test` in mods/measure-guard exits 1, and plan.md:10 lists that command. The record is honest and every count matches a fresh run, so this is wording only. Narrow plan.md:16 to the suites that ran, or fold the edit into the closeout plan edit. Rationale: A5 forbids an all-pass claim that a cited command contradicts.

F4 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The FR-7 tests do not cover three wrong-refusal classes, and the literal spec rules refuse all three. A backslash line continuation (`bun test` ending in a backslash, then a file on the next line) splits at the newline and is refused. A heredoc body line that starts with `bun test` is refused. `bun test --help`, `pytest --version`, `vitest --version`, and `bun test tests` have no file-like operand and are refused. The deny line names the heavy-run form and `/measure-off`, so a role agent recovers in one retry. Record the classes as accepted limits in the tech-debt row. Rationale: a wrong refusal costs one retry and loses no data.

F5 [Nit] phase-acceptance: Some direct heavy forms still pass, and the spec does not name them as v1 gaps. `sleep 1 & vite` passes because a single `&` does not split. `for x in a; do vite; done` and `(vite)` pass because argv[0] is a shell word. `sudo vite` passes because `sudo` is a wrapper word. A redirect target counts as a file operand under the FR-3 rule, so `bun test` with a redirect to `out.txt` passes (read from `hasFileOperand`, not run). Add these forms to the wrapper-gap tech-debt row. Rationale: each form is a path for a load-watch escape like the named gaps.

F6 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The plugin README `## Guards` section (plugins/opencode-measure-guard/README.md:66-78) lists each guard but not the heavy-run guard. Add this item to the F2 tech-debt row with the README.md:148-154 check lines. Rationale: a reader of the README cannot learn why a bare `bun test` is refused.
